newsitem.title: FRANCE: GOLF-HOLDER ALLENBY DISQUALIFIED IN FRANCE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-HOLDER ALLENBY DISQUALIFIED IN FRANCE.

text.p: Titleholder Robert Allenby of Australia was dramatically disqualified from the rain-affected French Open in Paris on Friday after signing for a wrong score.

The 26-year-old from Melbourne, who beat German Bernhard Langer in a playoff last year, signed for a par three on the 11th when he had taken four shots and was disqualified when the error came to light.

Tournament favourite Colin Montgomerie was Allenby's marker, unwittingly entering the wrong score, but the Australian was already struggling to make the halfway cut after signing for a five-over-par 77 which should have been 78.

"It was a straight case of miscounting, my fault entirely," said Allenby. "When I spoke to my caddie on the practice range and added up again, I realised my mistake. It is the second time I've done this and the second time here. I did a similar thing two years ago here."
It was a chastening experience for Allenby, who had flown in his parents this week to see the course where he triumphed last year.

Montgomerie carded 66 to move within two strokes of the first round leader Retief Goosen of South Africa, who posted an eight-under-par 64 after resuming his first round in the morning following Thursday's rain-affected day.
The second round began late on Friday afternoon.
